label: sparse conjunction around z/n/h/0 prefixes (unexplained)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.05% of steps). It is concentrated in sequences that start with z, n or g. It fires in the original phase at t=2-5, peaking at t=3 on h or 0 after an n n / z n prefix, and in the copy phase mostly when the input is z (often recall_idx 1, where z is fed back). The strongest examples are prefixes like n n 0 [h], z n n [h], and z z n <DEL> [z]. The broad predicate (input z, or original phase t>=2 in a sequence starting with z/n) captures about 77% of activation mass, but precision is about 1%. Narrower conjunctions over specific prefix tokens (orig(0), orig(1), prev2_tok) reach only about 8% precision with low recall. Windowed counts of the tokens {z,n,h,0,g,q} do no better. No predicate that was tried isolates the specific token combinations the feature needs. It never fires at t=0 or t=1, and rarely at the delimiter step.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=z (+6.76), phase=2 & in_tok=t (+3.95), phase=2 & in_tok=e (+3.67), prev_tok=h (+3.31), orig0=z (+3.28), orig0=n (+3.24). Lower it: to_go=7 (-4.37), prev_tok=w (-2.24), L=9 & recall_idx=-1 (-2.14), orig_idx=-1 (-1.98).
